claims.claim: **Outlook depends on where the vein is blocked and how ischaemic the retina is:** distal, less ischaemic occlusions do better. Central and hemi-central occlusions behave alike, are linked with glaucoma and carry more risk of anterior-segment new vessels and neovascular glaucoma than branch occlusions, so keep eye pressure controlled.
claims.locator: American Academy of Ophthalmology PPP Retina/Vitreous Committee (Kovach JL et al.), Ophthalmology, 'Retinal Vein Occlusions Preferred Practice Pattern (2024, updated 2026)', approved 13 September 2024; published Feb 2025; updated June 2026 (doi 10.1016/j.ophtha.2024.12.025), https://www.aao.org/education/preferred-practice-pattern/retinal-vein-occlusions-ppp, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **The first examination and imaging should decide:** branch, hemi or central occlusion; whether there is macular oedema; how much ischaemia; and whether new vessels are present on the retina or iris.
claims.locator: American Academy of Ophthalmology PPP Retina/Vitreous Committee (Kovach JL et al.), Ophthalmology, 'Retinal Vein Occlusions Preferred Practice Pattern (2024, updated 2026)', approved 13 September 2024; published Feb 2025; updated June 2026 (doi 10.1016/j.ophtha.2024.12.025), https://www.aao.org/education/preferred-practice-pattern/retinal-vein-occlusions-ppp, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Examine for:** a relative afferent pupillary defect (reflects ischaemia and predicts new vessels); fine new iris vessels on slit lamp; pressure; and gonioscopy before dilating, above all in ischaemic central occlusion, raised pressure or high risk of iris new vessels.
claims.locator: American Academy of Ophthalmology PPP Retina/Vitreous Committee (Kovach JL et al.), Ophthalmology, 'Retinal Vein Occlusions Preferred Practice Pattern (2024, updated 2026)', approved 13 September 2024; published Feb 2025; updated June 2026 (doi 10.1016/j.ophtha.2024.12.025), https://www.aao.org/education/preferred-practice-pattern/retinal-vein-occlusions-ppp, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **OCT is the key test for finding and measuring macular oedema, and it drives decisions to re-inject or change treatment**, though retinal thickness does not always match visual acuity.
claims.locator: American Academy of Ophthalmology PPP Retina/Vitreous Committee (Kovach JL et al.), Ophthalmology, 'Retinal Vein Occlusions Preferred Practice Pattern (2024, updated 2026)', approved 13 September 2024; published Feb 2025; updated June 2026 (doi 10.1016/j.ophtha.2024.12.025), https://www.aao.org/education/preferred-practice-pattern/retinal-vein-occlusions-ppp, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Fluorescein angiography needs informed consent (death occurs in about 1 in 200,000).** Ask women of childbearing age about pregnancy and breastfeeding and use it only when truly needed.
claims.locator: American Academy of Ophthalmology PPP Retina/Vitreous Committee (Kovach JL et al.), Ophthalmology, 'Retinal Vein Occlusions Preferred Practice Pattern (2024, updated 2026)', approved 13 September 2024; published Feb 2025; updated June 2026 (doi 10.1016/j.ophtha.2024.12.025), https://www.aao.org/education/preferred-practice-pattern/retinal-vein-occlusions-ppp, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Work with the GP:** RVO raises the risk of an occlusion in the other eye and of cardiovascular disease and stroke. **Under 50, consider haematology or general-medicine referral for a clotting work-up.**
claims.locator: American Academy of Ophthalmology PPP Retina/Vitreous Committee (Kovach JL et al.), Ophthalmology, 'Retinal Vein Occlusions Preferred Practice Pattern (2024, updated 2026)', approved 13 September 2024; published Feb 2025; updated June 2026 (doi 10.1016/j.ophtha.2024.12.025), https://www.aao.org/education/preferred-practice-pattern/retinal-vein-occlusions-ppp, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Hypertension accounts for about 48% of RVO, high lipids 20% and diabetes 5%.** Control them, although it is unproven that doing so improves vision or complications.
claims.locator: American Academy of Ophthalmology PPP Retina/Vitreous Committee (Kovach JL et al.), Ophthalmology, 'Retinal Vein Occlusions Preferred Practice Pattern (2024, updated 2026)', approved 13 September 2024; published Feb 2025; updated June 2026 (doi 10.1016/j.ophtha.2024.12.025), https://www.aao.org/education/preferred-practice-pattern/retinal-vein-occlusions-ppp, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Intravitreal anti-VEGF is first-line for macular oedema in both branch and central occlusion.** Intravitreal steroids work but are second-line because they cause glaucoma and cataract; laser has a limited role in branch occlusion.
claims.locator: American Academy of Ophthalmology PPP Retina/Vitreous Committee (Kovach JL et al.), Ophthalmology, 'Retinal Vein Occlusions Preferred Practice Pattern (2024, updated 2026)', approved 13 September 2024; published Feb 2025; updated June 2026 (doi 10.1016/j.ophtha.2024.12.025), https://www.aao.org/education/preferred-practice-pattern/retinal-vein-occlusions-ppp, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Four anti-VEGF agents are in routine use:** ranibizumab, aflibercept 2 mg and faricimab (FDA-approved) and bevacizumab (off-label, with supporting evidence). In trials, 8 mg of aflibercept given 8-weekly was noninferior to 4-weekly 2 mg, after 3–5 monthly loading doses.
claims.locator: American Academy of Ophthalmology PPP Retina/Vitreous Committee (Kovach JL et al.), Ophthalmology, 'Retinal Vein Occlusions Preferred Practice Pattern (2024, updated 2026)', approved 13 September 2024; published Feb 2025; updated June 2026 (doi 10.1016/j.ophtha.2024.12.025), https://www.aao.org/education/preferred-practice-pattern/retinal-vein-occlusions-ppp, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do not delay treatment.** In BRAVO, eyes first given sham and treated later never caught up with eyes treated from the start.
claims.locator: American Academy of Ophthalmology PPP Retina/Vitreous Committee (Kovach JL et al.), Ophthalmology, 'Retinal Vein Occlusions Preferred Practice Pattern (2024, updated 2026)', approved 13 September 2024; published Feb 2025; updated June 2026 (doi 10.1016/j.ophtha.2024.12.025), https://www.aao.org/education/preferred-practice-pattern/retinal-vein-occlusions-ppp, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Faricimab:** in BALATON (branch) and COMINO (central), 6 monthly doses of faricimab 6 mg were noninferior to aflibercept 2 mg for vision at week 24; treatment then moved to treat-and-extend at intervals of up to 16 weeks.
claims.locator: American Academy of Ophthalmology PPP Retina/Vitreous Committee (Kovach JL et al.), Ophthalmology, 'Retinal Vein Occlusions Preferred Practice Pattern (2024, updated 2026)', approved 13 September 2024; published Feb 2025; updated June 2026 (doi 10.1016/j.ophtha.2024.12.025), https://www.aao.org/education/preferred-practice-pattern/retinal-vein-occlusions-ppp, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Expect long treatment:** about half of branch and 56% to 75% of central occlusions still need anti-VEGF for oedema more than 5 years after starting.
claims.locator: American Academy of Ophthalmology PPP Retina/Vitreous Committee (Kovach JL et al.), Ophthalmology, 'Retinal Vein Occlusions Preferred Practice Pattern (2024, updated 2026)', approved 13 September 2024; published Feb 2025; updated June 2026 (doi 10.1016/j.ophtha.2024.12.025), https://www.aao.org/education/preferred-practice-pattern/retinal-vein-occlusions-ppp, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Before every intravitreal injection, use a topical antiseptic such as povidone-iodine;** routine antibiotic drops are not advised. Serious injection harms are uncommon: endophthalmitis, cataract, retinal detachment, raised pressure.
claims.locator: American Academy of Ophthalmology PPP Retina/Vitreous Committee (Kovach JL et al.), Ophthalmology, 'Retinal Vein Occlusions Preferred Practice Pattern (2024, updated 2026)', approved 13 September 2024; published Feb 2025; updated June 2026 (doi 10.1016/j.ophtha.2024.12.025), https://www.aao.org/education/preferred-practice-pattern/retinal-vein-occlusions-ppp, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Systemic safety:** anti-VEGF drugs carry a theoretical risk of arterial clots, but meta-analyses have not shown more major cardiovascular events or deaths.
claims.locator: American Academy of Ophthalmology PPP Retina/Vitreous Committee (Kovach JL et al.), Ophthalmology, 'Retinal Vein Occlusions Preferred Practice Pattern (2024, updated 2026)', approved 13 September 2024; published Feb 2025; updated June 2026 (doi 10.1016/j.ophtha.2024.12.025), https://www.aao.org/education/preferred-practice-pattern/retinal-vein-occlusions-ppp, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Branch occlusion: start with anti-VEGF.** Consider steroids and/or grid laser when the response fails or falls short.
claims.locator: American Academy of Ophthalmology PPP Retina/Vitreous Committee (Kovach JL et al.), Ophthalmology, 'Retinal Vein Occlusions Preferred Practice Pattern (2024, updated 2026)', approved 13 September 2024; published Feb 2025; updated June 2026 (doi 10.1016/j.ophtha.2024.12.025), https://www.aao.org/education/preferred-practice-pattern/retinal-vein-occlusions-ppp, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Steroid options:** in SCORE (central occlusion), triamcinolone 1 mg was preferred to 4 mg, which caused the most cataract and pressure rise. The dexamethasone implant's benefit rose from day 30, peaked at 90 days and was gone by 6 months; COBALT re-treated as often as every 4 months in branch occlusion.
claims.locator: American Academy of Ophthalmology PPP Retina/Vitreous Committee (Kovach JL et al.), Ophthalmology, 'Retinal Vein Occlusions Preferred Practice Pattern (2024, updated 2026)', approved 13 September 2024; published Feb 2025; updated June 2026 (doi 10.1016/j.ophtha.2024.12.025), https://www.aao.org/education/preferred-practice-pattern/retinal-vein-occlusions-ppp, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Overall, pressure rise and cataract with steroids make anti-VEGF the better first treatment.**
claims.locator: American Academy of Ophthalmology PPP Retina/Vitreous Committee (Kovach JL et al.), Ophthalmology, 'Retinal Vein Occlusions Preferred Practice Pattern (2024, updated 2026)', approved 13 September 2024; published Feb 2025; updated June 2026 (doi 10.1016/j.ophtha.2024.12.025), https://www.aao.org/education/preferred-practice-pattern/retinal-vein-occlusions-ppp, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Grid laser can be considered in branch occlusion with a perfused macula, oedema and vision of 20/40 or worse,** but anti-VEGF gives more gain and is preferred unless contraindicated. Laser suits patients who cannot attend monthly (review 3 months later). Adding laser to anti-VEGF gives no extra benefit.
claims.locator: American Academy of Ophthalmology PPP Retina/Vitreous Committee (Kovach JL et al.), Ophthalmology, 'Retinal Vein Occlusions Preferred Practice Pattern (2024, updated 2026)', approved 13 September 2024; published Feb 2025; updated June 2026 (doi 10.1016/j.ophtha.2024.12.025), https://www.aao.org/education/preferred-practice-pattern/retinal-vein-occlusions-ppp, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Central occlusion: focal laser does not help the macular oedema** (CVOS).
claims.locator: American Academy of Ophthalmology PPP Retina/Vitreous Committee (Kovach JL et al.), Ophthalmology, 'Retinal Vein Occlusions Preferred Practice Pattern (2024, updated 2026)', approved 13 September 2024; published Feb 2025; updated June 2026 (doi 10.1016/j.ophtha.2024.12.025), https://www.aao.org/education/preferred-practice-pattern/retinal-vein-occlusions-ppp, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Neovascularisation:** in branch occlusion with retinal new vessels, laser the non-perfused area to cut the risk of vitreous haemorrhage. In central occlusion with retinal or iris new vessels, give dense peripheral panretinal laser. An anti-VEGF injection first gives short-term control and can make full laser easier.
claims.locator: American Academy of Ophthalmology PPP Retina/Vitreous Committee (Kovach JL et al.), Ophthalmology, 'Retinal Vein Occlusions Preferred Practice Pattern (2024, updated 2026)', approved 13 September 2024; published Feb 2025; updated June 2026 (doi 10.1016/j.ophtha.2024.12.025), https://www.aao.org/education/preferred-practice-pattern/retinal-vein-occlusions-ppp, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Central occlusion: check the iris and angle (undilated slit lamp and gonioscopy) as often as monthly for 6 months,** and again in ischaemic central occlusion after anti-VEGF stops, to catch new vessels early.
claims.locator: American Academy of Ophthalmology PPP Retina/Vitreous Committee (Kovach JL et al.), Ophthalmology, 'Retinal Vein Occlusions Preferred Practice Pattern (2024, updated 2026)', approved 13 September 2024; published Feb 2025; updated June 2026 (doi 10.1016/j.ophtha.2024.12.025), https://www.aao.org/education/preferred-practice-pattern/retinal-vein-occlusions-ppp, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Refer every patient to their GP for the systemic conditions, share the results, and tell both about the risk to the other eye.** Offer counselling, vision rehabilitation and social support when vision is lost despite treatment.
claims.locator: American Academy of Ophthalmology PPP Retina/Vitreous Committee (Kovach JL et al.), Ophthalmology, 'Retinal Vein Occlusions Preferred Practice Pattern (2024, updated 2026)', approved 13 September 2024; published Feb 2025; updated June 2026 (doi 10.1016/j.ophtha.2024.12.025), https://www.aao.org/education/preferred-practice-pattern/retinal-vein-occlusions-ppp, retrieved 2026-09-23
